items.title: Alleged murderer thought he was being robbed during drug deal, jury told
paras: Liam Slann has admitted to killing Mr Holdback, but has denied it was an act of murder. ( Supplied: Facebook )
Liam Slann and his father, Brian Slann, are standing trial over the alleged murder of 21-year-old William Holdback.
Both men have pleaded not guilty to murder, but Liam Slann has entered a guilty plea to manslaughter, which the prosecution did not accept.
On Tuesday, Liam Slann took the stand to give evidence, saying it was "very unlucky" where his alleged victim was stabbed.
An Adelaide man has given evidence in his own murder trial, telling a jury he wanted to "get back" at a man who had swung a knife at him during an attempted drug deal.
Liam Slann and his father, Brian Slann, are standing trial for the murder of 21-year-old William Holdback, after a disagreement over drugs in April 2024.
Both men have pleaded not guilty to murder, but Liam Slann has entered a guilty plea to manslaughter, which the prosecution did not accept.
The prosecution previously alleged that William Holdback (pictured) was stabbed 10 times and left crying for help in Welland after a disagreement about drugs. ( Supplied: SA Police )
On Tuesday, Liam Slann took the stand telling the court he was worried and angry after he thought he was being robbed during the deal.
Liam Slann told the court he asked his father to drive him to the deal in Welland in Adelaide's inner north-west.
"It wasn't really a thing that Dad liked doing, but I asked him to do it anyway," he told the jury.
Liam Slann said the alleged victim approached the car wearing a COVID mask, asked to see the drugs, grabbed the bag of cocaine and swung a knife at him before the knife dropped into the car.
"His hand came straight through the window, came straight for my face," Liam Slann said.
He told the court the alleged victim smashed his dad's back window and taunted him.
The trial is being heard in South Australia's Supreme Court. ( ABC News: Che Chorley )
The court heard that Liam Slann jumped out of the car and said to the alleged victim, "You're f****** c**** … I'm going to stab you."
Liam Slann told the court he chased Mr Holdback, "trying to get the coke back".
Liam Slann told the court that when he caught up with the victim, Mr Holdback swung his skateboard at him before he [Liam Slann] lunged at him with the knife.
Defence barrister Elizabeth Mansfield is acting for Liam Slann. ( ABC News: Che Chorley )
When his lawyer, Elizabeth Mansfield, asked about what he wanted to do when he eventually caught up with the alleged victim, Liam Slann said he wanted to "hurt him".
"[In] reality, obviously hurt him … only to the extent of what happened … very unlucky where he got stabbed," he said.
The accused told the jury he remembered stabbing the alleged victim's shoulder but that his memory became hazy after that.
The court previously heard Mr Holdback was stabbed 10 times and was left crying out for help on the street.
When asked about his recollections after the stabbing, Liam Slann said he had been "in shock".
"I remember seeing him face down; it was a feeling that I'd never like to feel again," he said.
William Holdback's mother (second from left) was surrounded by supporters on the first day of the trial. ( ABC News: Che Chorley )
Under cross-examination, prosecutor Nicola Moore asked Liam Slann about CCTV that captured his father asking him where he stabbed Mr Holdback, to which the son replied "everywhere".
The prosecutor put to Liam Slann that he left the house with the knife before the alleged murder.
"You left the house, in the early hours of the morning, with a knife," Ms Moore said to the accused.
"That was one of the things you would take with you if you were meeting somebody in the early hours …"
"No, that's not correct. That's not right at all," Liam Slann responded.

items.title: Unemployment falls – for now
paras: Later this morning, former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn will release his report on the crisis of young people doing nothing. His solutions to the Neets problem will include new school readiness targets, more apprenticeships, better mental health support, a new benefit system for under-25s and the foundation of a ‘Youth Opportunity Service’.

Before that, though, the government has had some good news by way of the Office for National Statistics (ONS). The latest labour market figures, released this morning, show unemployment unexpectedly fell to 4.6 per cent, while 20,000 new payrolled jobs were created between August and September.
There was good news on youth unemployment too, which fell for the second month in a row to 15 per cent – the lowest rate in more than a year.

These figures buck the trend of job destruction kicked into gear by the £25 million national insurance raid and hikes to the minimum wage. Together these policies have contributed to 200,000 fewer payrolled jobs since Labour took office.
Nevertheless, today’s figures from the ONS, with the unemployment rate at its lowest since August 2025, point to a tighter jobs market than many had expected.

On wages, the pace of pay rises slowed in September, which will reduce pressure on the Bank of England to yet again hike interest rates. Wage growth fell to 3.5 per cent – down from 3.7 per cent the month before. This, the ONS said, was driven by a fall in public sector wage growth that has been elevated for the last few months.

The good news, I’m afraid, stops there, though. A ‘flash estimate’ of the payroll data shows a fall of 34,000 in September – the largest single-month drop since November 2020. Vacancies fell too to their lowest level – outside of lockdowns – since 2014.

Elsewhere, business costs increase and inflation data, which will be released tomorrow, is likely to show those costs are only going in one direction. The response from employers will be obvious: another slowdown in hiring. So the government can thank their lucky stars that they’ve started the day of Milburn’s launch with relatively good economic news. But it’s not going to last.

items.title: How infamous fraudster Sam Bankman-Fried missed out on a $52 billion jackpot
paras: Advertisement Business Companies Wall Street How infamous fraudster Sam Bankman-Fried missed out on a $52 billion jackpot David Yaffe-Bellany November 17, 2026 — 6:15pm
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A Sam Bankman-Fried, the convicted cryptocurrency fraudster , lives in a 30-person unit at the federal prison in Lompoc, California, a barbed-wire compound about a million miles away from his former life as a technology billionaire in the Bahamas.
For the most part, Bankman-Fried, 34, tries not to think about all the “could-have-beens,” he said on a recent call. But one has become difficult to ignore.

Before FTX filed for bankruptcy, Bankman-Fried was worth an estimated $US24 billion, giving him tremendous influence in business and politics. AP In late 2021, the heyday of his FTX crypto exchange, Bankman-Fried spent $US500 million ($742 million) on a 13.5 per cent stake in a little-known artificial intelligence startup called Anthropic. This week, Anthropic is set for an initial public offering that is expected to value the company at $US1.4 trillion, potentially one of the largest Wall Street debuts in history.
At that valuation, Bankman-Fried’s investment, diluted over several years, would now be worth an eye-watering $US35 billion — about the size of FTX’s entire business at its peak.

But the shares are gone. They were tied up in bankruptcy court until 2024, when executives overseeing the scattered remains of FTX sold the Anthropic stake for $US1.34 billion — a tiny fraction of its current value.

For Anthropic, the fate of those shares is an odd quirk of history. For Bankman-Fried, it’s a source of extreme frustration and resentment. Even after a fraud conviction , a failed appeal and a succession of public humiliations, he is still trying to prove his innocence, arguing that FTX had sufficient resources to avoid bankruptcy.
“There’s no point in obsessing over regrets,” he said. “But it’s certainly something that I’ve spent, despite that, a fair bit of time thinking through.”

In September, Bankman-Fried submitted the longest of long-shot appeals to the Supreme Court, where he cited the Anthropic investment. He claimed that the judge in his trial had improperly prevented him from arguing that FTX had enough money to repay its users.

But none of his arguments was ever likely to overcome the basic facts of FTX’s collapse, an epic financial fraud that drew instant comparisons to Bernie Madoff’s Ponzi scheme. Bankman-Fried gave up control of FTX in November 2022, after a run on deposits exposed an $US8 billion hole in customer accounts. A year later, he was convicted on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy. He had used the missing money to buy luxury real estate, donate to political campaigns and invest in startups like Anthropic.

Ultimately, the return on those investments proved irrelevant, as far as guilt and innocence were concerned. In US District Court for the Southern District of New York, Judge Lewis A. Kaplan memorably compared Bankman-Fried to a “thief who takes his loot to Las Vegas and successfully bets the stolen money.” He sentenced him to 25 years in prison.

Anthropic is set to list on Wall Street this week. Michael Nagle “Mr. Bankman-Fried conveniently skips over the fact that he misappropriated and gambled with customer moneys,” John Ray, a corporate turnaround expert who oversaw the bankruptcy, said in a statement. “We are proud of the integrity and impact of the work we have done with our large team of committed professionals.”

Before FTX filed for bankruptcy, Bankman-Fried was worth an estimated $US24 billion, giving him tremendous influence in business and politics. His company was one of the world’s largest crypto exchanges, a venue where customers could buy, sell and store digital coins.

Bankman-Fried was also a leading practitioner of “effective altruism,” a philanthropic movement that focuses on combating threats that might emerge decades or centuries in the future. Like many effective altruists, Bankman-Fried was concerned about the dangers of out-of-control AI long before it became a major talking point in American politics.

Those views aligned him with Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, who moved in the same effective altruist circles. Amodei started the AI company after leaving a rival, OpenAI, in late 2020 amid disagreements over how to make the technology safer.

Bankman-Fried said he spoke with Amodei not long after that, when FTX was based in Hong Kong. “I was one degree removed and knew a number of people who knew him,” Bankman-Fried recalled. Amodei struck him as “really intelligent, dedicated, very knowledgeable.”
In April 2022, Anthropic announced the investment from Bankman-Fried and two of his FTX colleagues, drawing little notice at the time.

“We cared about AI companies being responsible, and preparing for AI to help rather than hurt society,” Bankman-Fried said on the phone from prison. “Anthropic seemed far more committed to that than the other major companies.”
Then in fall 2022, FTX plunged into crisis, exposing a giant theft of customer money. Three weeks later, OpenAI released its ChatGPT chatbot, setting off an AI frenzy.
Within a year, Bankman-Fried had been convicted, while Anthropic was raising billions of dollars from high-profile investors like Amazon. It had recently released a popular chatbot, Claude.
As Anthropic turned into one of Silicon Valley’s hottest startups, the fate of Bankman-Fried’s shares became a subject of intense debate in Delaware bankruptcy court.

When FTX failed, Bankman-Fried had handed control to Ray, who had managed the unwinding of Enron. Working with the law firm Sullivan & Cromwell, Ray set out to raise funds to pay back FTX customers in full. Bankman-Fried had left a messy assortment of corporate assets, including obscure digital coins, properties in the Bahamas and shares in other companies.

Ray’s team started looking for buyers. A wide-ranging sale is typical in any corporate bankruptcy, where the job of the estate is to maximise recoveries as efficiently as possible. But some customers wanted FTX to sit on the Anthropic stake for longer.
“I wish they held onto it,” said Sunil Kavuri, an FTX customer who testified at Bankman-Fried’s sentencing. “I foresaw that it would be one of the most valuable assets.”
It didn’t help that Ray came across as misinformed about the potential value of the shares. In an interview with author Michael Lewis, he dismissed the company as “this thing called Anthropic.”

In the end, FTX sold the Anthropic stake at about $US30 per share to a few dozen investors, who paid $US1.34 billion, according to court filings. The buyers included a business entity linked to Mubadala, the United Arab Emirates investment fund; the nonprofit Ford Foundation; and the trading firm Jane Street, which once employed Bankman-Fried.
A spokesperson for the FTX estate said the sale of the Anthropic stake was “conducted through a court-supervised process and achieved market value at the time”.

The collapse of FTX sent shockwaves through the world of crypto. AP “Billions of stolen funds were misappropriated and invested, without customer consent,” the spokesperson said. “There was no way to know at that time whether those investments would succeed or fail and many did fail.”
Representatives for Jane Street and the Ford Foundation declined to comment. Mubadala did not respond to a request for comment.

A bankruptcy estate has significant leeway to decide when and how to sell its assets. Under the circumstances, FTX’s handling of the Anthropic shares was reasonable, said Lindsey Simon, a professor at Emory University School of Law.
“At the time, there was no news about an IPO,” Simon said. “Now we know that they became extraordinarily valuable. But what if they had turned into nothing?”

In May 2024, the estate announced that FTX’s creditors were set to receive as much as $US1.18 for every dollar they lost when the exchange failed — more than a full repayment. But that has not quieted the complaints.

The promised returns were pegged to the value of crypto at the time FTX collapsed, when the market was in a deep slump. If customers held bitcoin on FTX on the day the company filed for bankruptcy, they would be compensated in line with the coin’s price at that moment — not its current price, which is several times higher.
“It was our money, and we didn’t give him rights to use our money,” Kavuri said. “It sucks.”

These days, Bankman-Fried has only limited contact with the outside world. He exchanges messages with a network of journalists, friends and relatives, who have kept him up-to-date on AI developments. Bankman-Fried can access the prison phones for 15 minutes at a time, before each call automatically ends.
Over several conversations this fall, he kept returning to Ray and the bankruptcy lawyers.
“I’m sure you could’ve come up with a way for them to manage it worse,” he said, “but I can’t think of one off the top of my head.”

Bankman-Fried was repeating grievances that have been repeatedly rejected in court. But does he ever ponder an alternate universe where FTX didn’t implode and the Anthropic shares made him incredibly wealthy?
“A little bit,” he said, starting to answer. “I try not to spend too much time. …”

items.title: Bikie admits to inquiry he may have charged Vic taxpayers for shifts not worked
paras: Bandidos bikie Joel Leavitt was called as a witness for the Big Build royal commission. ( Supplied )
Under sustained questioning, Bandidos bikie Joel Leavitt told Victoria's Big Build royal commission he could not recall events in 2021 and 2022.
The inquiry heard evidence the CFMEU had pushed a construction company to employ Mr Leavitt on a state government building project.
Mr Leavitt also admitted to the commission it was possible he charged taxpayers for shifts he did not work.
Text messages have been shown to Victoria's Big Build royal commission exposing the efforts of a CFMEU organiser to ensure a bikie was hired on a government building site.

In its seventh day of hearings, the royal commission into alleged corruption on major public projects called on current member of outlaw motorcycle gang the Bandidos and former member of the Rebels, Joel Leavitt, to give evidence.

Various text messages between Mr Leavitt and CFMEU (Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union) organiser Jerry McQuaid were read out which showed the union wanted Mr Leavitt hired as a labourer on a Big Build project in Melbourne's south-east for construction company Laing O'Rourke.
Counsel Assisting Chris Carr SC appeared frustrated at times with Mr Leavitt's lack of recollection of events. ( Supplied )
The messages showed Mr McQuaid's persistence over a series of months from November 2021 and suggested Laing O'Rourke showed resistance, refusing to employ the bikie on the Cranbourne site.
In one message Mr McQuaid wrote to Mr Leavitt that the CFMEU was "pushing like f***".
In another message, Mr McQuaid said he had "been walloping them all week".
The inquiry heard when the contractor did not comply, the union launched an industrial campaign against them.
Mr McQuaid wrote in one message "Joe's abused the f*** out of them and we're all going there to play up tomorrow".
It was suggested that the company did not want to hire Mr Leavitt because of his criminal record, which included riot, affray and assault charges.
Asked what qualities Mr Leavitt had for the CFMEU to push "incredibly hard" to have him employed on a job site, Mr Leavitt replied "I'm a good bloke".
"One possibility might be that the CFMEU wanted to go to such lengths to get you on this job site because you're an intimidating bikie," counsel assisting the commission Chris Carr SC said.
Mr Leavitt admitted it was possible he had charged taxpayers for shifts on the Cranbourne rail project when he was not at work.

The inquiry was shown some of Mr Leavitt's time sheets claiming hours of work as a health and safety representative (HSR), which did not appear to match his phone records — which showed him either at the gym or home.

At one stage, the commissioner and counsel assisting had Mr Leavitt write "HSR" six times on a piece of paper to see if it matched the handwriting on his time sheet, because he had claimed he could not recall whether or not he wrote it.
Under questioning from commissioner Chris Kourakis, Mr Leavitt said he could not remember seeking payments for hours that did not match his phone record.
Mr Leavitt: There is potential that that could have happened. I can't recall to that time.
Mr Kourakis: What you recall about the man you were back then, was that you wouldn't rule out and you can't rule out that you claimed for hours you didn't work?
Throughout the inquiry, Mr Leavitt told the commission he could not recall many events from 2021 and 2022.
It prompted the commissioner to ask if he had been diagnosed with any cognitive decline or had seen a medical practitioner about his apparent lack of recollection of events.
He admitted he was a heavy drug user at the time and "in different hazy states".
The hearing continues tomorrow, when Mr Leavitt is expected to return to give more evidence.

items.title: Why I won’t miss Emma Barnett on the Today programme
paras: It was confirmed yesterday that presenter Emma Barnett is to leave the Today programme, and focus her talents instead on a new multi-platform programme for the BBC starting early next year. What this new show actually involves, and exactly which platforms it will be spreading itself across, remains a mystery. (I think multi-platform is just a fancy way of saying ‘podcast’.) But I’m afraid I can’t say I am sorry to hear of her departure.
Like many formerly essential BBC properties, in the last decade or so Today has gone from a ‘must listen’ to a ‘must avoid’

Today has had a unique spot in the current affairs firmament since its inception. It will – staggeringly – reach its 70th birthday next year. But like many formerly essential BBC properties, in the last decade or so it has gone from a ‘must listen’ to a ‘must avoid’.

Actually, ‘must avoid’ is too strong; I find that it simply no longer occurs to me to tune in. I was always a Radio 2 breakfast show man – and don’t get my motor revving on what’s happened to that – but I could be, and frequently was, tempted to twiddle my dial to Today when especially big or interesting news stories were in the air. Now? I find the thought never arises.

On the rare occasions when I did encounter the show during Barnett’s short tenure – just over two years – she struck me as a bad fit. The long shadow of John Humphrys still hangs over Today. Humphrys, like Jeremy Paxman, could be combative and impatient with guests, but you always felt that they deserved it. With Barnett, it feels like she is doing what is expected. She has had some spectacular encounters of the ‘when did you stop beating your wife?’ variety, not least of which was her interview with Kemi Badenoch a few weeks ago. She opened with the inane bleat of ‘Are you willing to make people homeless in the name of national defence?’, and things didn’t improve from there.

It strikes me that Barnett is just not a morning person, not a bright sunbeam of the dawn. While previous holders of her position like Sarah Montague or Sue MacGregor did occasionally get quite firm, they sounded like they wanted to be there. The Barnett vibe is more teenage bedhead, of the grouchy, ‘I’ve just woken up, Mum’ variety.

But the problems of Today cannot be laid at the door of any individual, and are not entirely the fault of the BBC. Many long-standing institutions are not equipped for the modern era. In an age of clipped-up current affairs ‘content’, shouty encounters between journalists and public figures are ten-a-penny. Younger readers won’t believe me, but these occasions used to be rare. Now? You’ll see about 20 before midday.

The main problem? The BBC shot itself in both feet by succumbing to the fashionable nonsense that swallowed up progressive politics in the early part of the last decade. It had, of course, always been left-liberal, but when truly potty ideas became part of that mix it didn’t even try to resist. We are all familiar with its long list of scandals in the period – the Jewish bus slur, its unquestioning adoption of transgenderism as a jolly good idea, the Gaza coverage provided by satellites of terrorists. Losing your authority is a disaster for any news organisation, but the BBC gaily threw away its gold standard reputation as if it didn’t matter. It is still purveying identity hokum – it recently published a very spurious article on ‘transphobia’ in football crowds.

And why? Well, because everybody else was doing it, Miss. Now, it was hardly a shock that the Beeb – whose staff, as anybody who has worked there can tell you, ranges from centrist extremist to extremist extremist – is an organ of the progressive establishment. What is galling, considering its funding model, is that it jumped into the truly cranky fringes the moment they became the mode. This has marked the BBC as unreliable and untrustworthy – the worst thing any news outlet can be. Find Out Now’s 2025 survey discovered, for the first time, that an outright majority do not trust its news content.

The BBC has let itself slide into the worst possible place in the new media era – too brain-numbingly PC for people like me, too milquetoast for progressives in comparison to full-throated, partisan podcasts from ex-staffers like The News Agents. No wonder Emma Barnett sounds so crabby.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "Trust but verify...," says former envoy KP Fabian on patrolling agreement between India-China along LAC
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): KP Fabian , former India n Ambassador to Canada, struck a cautious note regarding the recent agreement between India and China on border patrolling along the Line of Actual Control ( LAC ), advising that while trust is essential, verification is equally important. While speaking with ANI, he said, "It's a very important statement that says that India and China have come to an agreement about normal patrolling and that there will be disengagement. The Foreign Secretary says that we are now looking at the resolution of the problem which arose in 2020." He added, "Some years ago, before a meeting, PM Narendra Modi was going to China for another international meeting. It (the issues) were resolved. But, let us recall that the Chinese did not carry out (the solution). The agreement was in two stages. In the first stage, India will withdraw first, then China will withdraw. That was done. In the second stage, China had to withdraw first, and then India , which they didn't do. Then, they constructed a lot of things. So, this step is welcome. Let me put it this way, trust but verify." The former diplomat further said that being neighbours, it is necessary for India and China to have "good neighbourly relations" if possible.

He said, " China is coming under a lot of pressure from the West. Americans are saying that China has been supporting Russia (with regard to the Russia-Ukraine conflict). Chinese electric vehicles are coming under high tariffs and so China is coming under pressure... And I believe that China and India , both being big countries but neighbours, it is necessary to have, if possible, good neighbourly relations." On Monday, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, said India and China have reached an agreement on the patrolling arrangements along LAC . The agreement was reached ahead of the BRICS Summit which will be attended by PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping . "On several areas along the Line of Actual Control , we held discussions with Chinese interlocutors, both on diplomatic as well as the military levels through meeting with military commanders at various levels. These discussions had in the past resulted in the resolution of standoffs at various locations. There are some locations and areas where stand-offs had not been resolved," said Misri. "Now, as a result of the discussions taking place over the last several weeks, an agreement has been arrived at on patrolling arrangements along the LAC in the India - China border areas. This is leading to disengagement and eventually a resolution of the issues that had arisen in these areas in 2020," he added. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: ATP Chiefs Under Fire For Skipping Doubles Trophy Presentation At Year-End Finals
paras: Henry Patten has criticised leading figures at the ATP for their absence from the year-end No. 1 doubles trophy presentation, which was presented to him and partner Harri Heliovaara. The British-Finnish duo was recognised for their achievements this season, including winning Wimbledon and reaching the French Open final.

They have also won four other titles since January. On Monday afternoon, the duo was presented with their trophy at the ATP Finals in Turin. However, both ATP chairman Andrea Guadenzi and CEO ​Eno Polo were not in attendance.

It’s a real shame that the ATP Chairman and the ATP CEO don’t think the same,” Patten said during his on-court speech. “It would have been nice to have them on court with us today. But here we are by ourselves, and we work incredibly hard, and thank you all for appreciating that.”

items.title: The five players who earned the most prize money on the WTA Tour in 2026 following Mirra Andreeva’s WTA Finals triumph
paras: Mirra Andreeva received a healthy sum after capturing her first WTA Finals title on Sunday. The Russian youngster, who went undefeated at the event, earned $3,370,000 for her efforts in Indian Wells, California.

Andreeva’s triumph in the US capped what has been a truly memorable year on the WTA Tour – one defined by the successes of Andreeva and three-time major champion Elena Rybakina. With the season coming to an end, let us take a look at the WTA’s final prize money standings for the year.

It has been a career-defining year for Kazakhstani star Elena Rybakina. The 27-year-old won two Grand Slam titles – the Australian Open and US Open – and captured the world number one ranking for the first time in her career. Which of these four WTA players will win the most Grand Slams next year?

items.title: Elina Svitolina now praises Mirra Andreeva and says what is ‘incredible’ about her after their WTA Finals match
paras: Mirra Andreeva played some of the best tennis of her career to win the WTA Finals title last week. The Russian youngster, only 19 years old, did not drop a set en route to winning the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina [twice], Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula.
Andreeva capped her impressive week with victory against Svitolina in Sunday’s final . The teenager triumphed 7-5, 6-3 in Indian Wells, California.

Svitolina, who also enjoyed an impressive campaign amid troubles in her personal life , heavily praised her triumphant opponent in the aftermath of Sunday’s showdown. “She [Andreeva] was serving better than me today as well. There were some points where I wish I could serve a bit better,” Svitolina said of Andreeva during her post-match press conference in California.

items.title: November 17, 1991: The day Pete Sampras claimed his first season-ending ATP Masters Cup
paras: On this day in tennis history, one young American beat a compatriot to win his first ATP Masters Cup.
On this day, November 17, 1991, in Frankfurt, Pete Sampras beat Jim Courier in the final (3-6, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4) to claim his first title at the season-ending Masters Cup .

For the young American, who had lost his US Open crown two months earlier – to the same opponent – it was a relief to win such an important title after a hard season. It was also the first of five titles claimed by the future world No 1 at the year-end Masters Cup, which would be a record at the time (eventually broken by Roger Federer in 2011). Although he was an integral part of a golden American generation, along with Andre Agassi, Michael Chang and Courier, he was the last of them to become an elite player.
items.impact: Courier’s career took off in 1991: after clinching the titles at both Indian Wells and Miami, he triumphed at Roland-Garros to everyone’s surprise, beating his rival Agassi in the final (3-6, 6-4, 2-6, 6-1, 6-4).

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
